artboards.title: Scoreboard B — rounds as rows (not chosen)

annotations.text:
DartiX 2.0 — Broadcast direction

Charcoal ground, condensed numerals, one amber accent. Amber and red are STATUS colours (active turn, leader, halving) and never identify a player; the charts on the Stats page use a separate validated series palette so the two never get confused.

The scoreboard is live — click the pad and play it out.

Layout decided: A — players as rows, the twelve rounds across, pad below the board.

Reads like a live leaderboard, takes any number of players, and uses a laptop's width instead of its height.

The rejected B layout is on the "Not chosen" page. One idea worth stealing from it: B showed the running total inside every cell, which makes it obvious where a halving bit. Say the word and I'll fold that into A as a toggle.

The pad is the biggest win over the old app, which shipped a 20px number input and two abandoned on-screen keypads.

Note the Doubles/Triples mode: tap the faces you hit and it does the arithmetic. The old app made you sum them in your head before typing.

The old Stats tab was three flat tables in an accordion plus one orange line chart.

Every number here is invented but internally consistent — the heatmap, the radar and the bleed chart all tell the same story about who owns which round. Swap in real data and the shapes will change; the layouts should not.
